Shrimp, as sold from water-soluble had dimethylarsinic acid higher at 470 µg/kg, against 10 µg/kg for lipid-soluble in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kaise T, Hanaoka K, Tagawa S, Hirayama T, Fukui S · 1988</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Distribution of inorganic arsenic and methylated arsenic in marine organisms</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the shrimp came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-shrimp" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-shrimp-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of shrimp, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:shrimp-0d1fbb755c7f:6716a09692d2"><summary>HMI shrimp Pb reference · Shrimp, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:shrimp-0d1fbb755c7f:6716a09692d2"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI shrimp Pb reference · Shrimp, as sold. Shrimp, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤15</td><td>33</td><td>33</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤15</td><td>33</td><td>33</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>66 reference units; 2 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>65</td><td>50%</td></tr><tr><td>Olmedo et al. 2013</td><td>1</td><td>50%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for shrimp, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach shrimp

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach shrimp comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Shrimp, as sold from water-soluble had dimethylarsinic acid higher at 470 µg/kg, against 10 µg/kg for lipid-soluble in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kaise T, Hanaoka K, Tagawa S, Hirayama T, Fukui S · 1988</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Distribution of inorganic arsenic and methylated arsenic in marine organisms</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, shrimp, frozen from frozen product (moisture 82%) had inorganic arsenic higher at 396 µg/kg, against 384 µg/kg for frozen product (moisture 82%) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/munoz1999-seafood-inorganic-arsenic|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Munoz O, Velez D, Cervera ML, Montoro R · 1999</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/munoz1999-seafood-inorganic-arsenic">Rapid and quantitative release, separation and determination of inorganic arsenic [As(III)+As(V)] in seafood products by microwave-assisted distillation and hydride generation atomic absorption spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Analytical Atomic Spectrometry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/munoz1999-seafood-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kaise T, Hanaoka K, Tagawa S, Hirayama T, Fukui S · 1988</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Distribution of inorganic arsenic and methylated arsenic in marine organisms</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, monomethylarsonic acid, total mercury, methylmercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, As, As(III), As(V), AsB, AsC, AsIII, AsSugar-OH, AsSugar-PO4, AsSugar-SO3, AsSugar-SO4, AsV, Cr(III), CrVI, DBT, DOT, DPhT, Hg, Hg-inorganic, I, MBT, Mo, MPhT, oAs, organotin_DBT, organotin_DPT, organotin_MBT, organotin_MPT, organotin_TBT, organotin_TPT, OTC_sum_as_Sn, Rb, Sr, sumBT, sumOTC, sumPhT, TBT, TBT+DBT+TPhT, TMA, TPhT, TPT and unknown As in shrimp, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-shrimp" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-shrimp" data-question="How do heavy metals get into shrimp?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into shrimp?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, shrimp from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than shrimp from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kaise T, Hanaoka K, Tagawa S, Hirayama T, Fukui S · 1988</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Distribution of inorganic arsenic and methylated arsenic in marine organisms</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Shrimp, as sold from Muscle had total arsenic higher at 65,800 µg/kg, against 13,600 µg/kg for Muscle in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kaise T, Hanaoka K, Tagawa S, Hirayama T, Fukui S · 1988</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Distribution of inorganic arsenic and methylated arsenic in marine organisms</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-shrimp-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-types-of-shrimp-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which types of shrimp have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of shrimp have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For lead, the HMI reference median was lowest for shrimp, cooked (4.2 µg/kg) and highest for shrimp, as sold (33 µg/kg); forms differ in water content, so this compares foods as sold or eaten, not uptake.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/olmedo2013-andalusia-fish-shellfish-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Olmedo P, Pla A, Hernandez AF, Barbier F, Ayouni L, Gil F · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/olmedo2013-andalusia-fish-shellfish-metals">Determination of toxic elements (mercury, cadmium, lead, tin and arsenic) in fish and shellfish samples. Risk assessment for the consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environment International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/olmedo2013-andalusia-fish-shellfish-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-shrimp" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-shrimp" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in shrimp?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in shrimp?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, shrimp, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in WPRO (5.77 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (121 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (5 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (500 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in shrimp is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">
